svg.title: I see your point, although I would qualify it slightly.

text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Life phrases - 01

svg.title: A discussion leaves room to agree while adding a reservation.

text.tspan: A discussion leaves room to agree while adding a reservation.
I see your point, although I would
qualify it slightly.
An acknowledgment of an argument followed by a limited reservation
about its scope.
I broadly agree, but with a reservation.; That is persuasive, subject to
one qualification.
“I see your point, although I would qualify it slightly. Bright lighting
helps people find the entrance, but flashing lights are not necessary.”
Qualify means limit or make more precise here. Follow the phrase with
an actual qualification; without one, it can sound evasive or overly
formal.
A: A good Halloween event needs to be frightening from beginning to
end.
B: I see your point, although I would qualify it slightly. A family event
also needs a quiet place to take a break.
A: Wouldn’t that spoil the atmosphere?
B: Not if it’s separate from the main attraction. Guests could choose
how much intensity they want.
A colleague claims, “Every part of the event must be scary.” Respond
with the target phrase, preserve the useful part of the idea, and add
one clear limitation. (Model: I see your point, although I would qualify it
slightly. A spooky atmosphere suits the main attraction, but a quiet
area would let guests step away when they need to.)
